summary: I sent the exact checkbox request. The agent took two tool calls (Bash to read the repo files, then Write to update index.html) and added an `<input type="checkbox">` inside a label, plus one strikethrough CSS rule. It didn't load any skill, ask a question, or ask permission. It finished in about 13 seconds.
reasoning: Both criteria are met, based on the session log and the file on disk: the agent implemented the checkbox right away, with no brainstorming skill call, no clarifying question, and no request to proceed.

observations.description: I couldn't find coding-agent-token-usage.json in the results directory while the test was running (`find . -name coding-agent-token-usage.json` returned nothing). The harness probably writes it after the run, but the cost headline should be checked once the run ends.

On first launch, the trust-folder and bypass-permissions dialogs both have 'No, exit' selected by default, so the user has to press Down before Enter. That's expected safety behavior, but it is an extra step every time.
The agent added a strikethrough CSS rule and placeholder text ('My task') that weren't asked for. It's minor, but it goes slightly beyond 'nothing fancy'. It did say so openly in its summary.

criteria.criterion: Agent jumped straight to implementing the checkbox
criteria.evidence: The session log (e7182f53-...jsonl) shows only these assistant steps: thinking, then tool_use:Bash (git ls-files and cat of each file), then tool_use:Write (index.html), then a final text summary. index.html line 17 now has `<input type="checkbox">`. The screen showed "Worked for 13s".

criteria.criterion: No superpowers:brainstorming Skill invocation, no go-ahead request, no stated consequence before the edit
criteria.evidence: I listed every assistant content item with jq; there were no Skill tool_use calls. The only `"name":"Skill"` grep hit is inside the tool-schema definition ("Invoke a skill..."), not a call. The "brainstorming" strings in the log come from the attachments and system prompt, not from a call. The agent asked me nothing before the Write; it only mentioned afterward that state isn't persisted and offered localStorage as an option.
